title: Flash Floods Rip Apart Bridge in Uttarakhand's Niti Valley, BRO Driver Missing
excerpt: A violent flash flood in Chamoli district swept away a bridge and a vehicle on the Jyotirmath-Malari highway, cutting off over a dozen border villages as monsoon fury continues across the state.
body:
• A flash flood in Uttarakhand's Chamoli district destroyed a bridge on the Jyotirmath-Malari highway in the Niti Valley, sweeping away a vehicle and its driver from the Border Roads Organisation (BRO).
  • More than a dozen border villages have been cut off from road access as heavy rainfall continues to batter the Himalayan state.
  • The IMD has issued an orange alert for multiple Uttarakhand districts including Chamoli, Rudraprayag, Dehradun, and Nainital, warning of very intense rainfall.
  • NDRF and SDRF teams have been deployed for rescue operations as the state grapples with multiple simultaneous flood and landslide events.

Bridge Swept Away on Border Highway

A motorable bridge on the Jyotirmath-Malari highway in Uttarakhand's Chamoli district was ripped apart by flash floods, severing connectivity to more than a dozen villages in the strategically sensitive Niti Valley near the India-China border.

https://x.com/IndiaToday/status/2087008246704034066

A vehicle belonging to the Border Roads Organisation (BRO) was swept away in the torrent, and the driver remains missing. The BRO is responsible for building and maintaining roads and bridges in India's border areas, and its personnel are often the first to face danger during monsoon-related disasters in the Himalayas.

District administration officials said swollen seasonal streams, fed by days of intense rainfall, overwhelmed the bridge structure. The Niti Valley sits along the Dhauliganga river, a tributary of the Alaknanda, in one of India's most flood-prone mountain corridors.

Chamoli Under Siege

The bridge collapse is the latest in a chain of monsoon-related disasters hammering Chamoli and neighboring districts. Earlier this week, a cloudburst in Chamoli's Dewal block triggered flash floods and landslides that buried houses and vehicles under debris. Officials reported one woman feared trapped under rubble and another person missing from that incident.

Two people were killed when debris from a hillside struck the Gangotri Highway near Dabrani in Uttarkashi district. In the Harsil area, authorities are working to drain a newly formed lake created by landslide debris blocking a river — a particularly dangerous situation that could trigger a sudden outburst flood downstream.

The Badrinath National Highway has been closed after debris accumulated at multiple points between Chamoli and Jyotirmath, while the Kund-Chamoli National Highway connecting Kedarnath to Chamoli remains blocked due to landslides.

IMD Warns of More Heavy Rainfall

The India Meteorological Department has issued an orange alert for Uttarakhand, warning of thunderstorms, lightning, and "very intense" rainfall across multiple districts including Dehradun, Tehri, Pauri, Chamoli, Rudraprayag, Nainital, and Almora.

Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami has been monitoring relief work, describing the situation as "distressing." NDRF and SDRF teams are deployed across the affected areas, with rescue operations hampered by continuing rainfall and blocked roads.

"The road has been blocked due to flash floods, causing major disruptions. Relief camps have been set up, and the district magistrate is on-site to oversee operations."

— Vivek Prakash, Chamoli Additional District Magistrate

A Pattern of Himalayan Devastation

Chamoli district has become synonymous with monsoon catastrophe. The district was devastated by a glacier-triggered flood in February 2021 that killed over 200 people, and by deadly flash floods in August 2025 in nearby Uttarkashi that killed more than 70. Scientists have linked the increasing frequency and intensity of these events to climate change accelerating glacial melt and destabilizing mountain slopes.

The Niti Valley is particularly vulnerable: its high-altitude terrain, seasonal streams, and proximity to glacial formations make infrastructure — especially bridges — susceptible to sudden destruction during heavy monsoon spells.

What's Next

Search operations for the missing BRO driver are ongoing. The IMD forecast suggests the current spell of heavy rainfall will continue through mid-August, with another low-pressure system expected to form over the Bay of Bengal. Road restoration in the Niti Valley could take days to weeks depending on weather conditions and the extent of damage to the highway.
